An award-winning education
WELCOME
St George’s is no ordinary school. With a heritage that dates back to 1348, this is a school with a pioneering vision, a determination to do things differently, and a community which is nurturing and above all else, kind. We look forward to welcoming you to our unique Real World Ready school.

Pioneering Curriculum
Our innovative teaching framework challenges students to think critically and take ownership of their own learning, focusing on asking the right questions rather than simply answering them.
READY FOR ADVENTURE
Round Square
St George’s is a proud member of Round Square, a network of more than 200 like-minded schools with a common purpose, fostering global thinking and international mindedness.
READY FOR LIFE
Wellbeing
Through a school-wide approach which prioritises mental wellbeing, we pride ourselves on nurturing children to be kind, resilient and well prepared for the world that waits beyond.
READY FOR LEARNING
Learning
Our pioneering International Baccalaureate-based curriculum challenges students to think critically and take ownership of their own learning, focusing on asking the right questions rather than simply answering them.

Co-curricular activities
With over 40 different clubs and activities on offer each term, our co-curricular programme encourages children to pursue their hobbies and passions and grow in confidence, independence and curiosity.
READY FOR LIFE
Wellbeing
Through a school-wide approach which prioritises mental wellbeing, we pride ourselves on nurturing children to be kind, resilient and well prepared for the world that waits beyond.
WHAT OTHERS SAY
Some schools are as grand as castles, but this one is attached to one. But that’s not what makes St George’s Windsor special – it has a visionary head, kindness is king and it maintains an impressive academic record.
Now a thriving co-ed with music at its core. But what really marks St George’s out is its commitment to pupils’ emotional wellbeing.

pageCache.text:
SCHOOLS IN PARTNERSHIP
St George’s is a registered charity with an overarching aim to ‘enhance the education of ALL children’. Our long-term ambition is to develop, sustain and promote an enduring partnership with other schools which will benefit staff and students, as well as the wider community. Our aim is for the partnership to be ‘mutually beneficial’ for all, and for all parties to collaborate and learn from each other through a rich professional learning community.
Through discussion we will promote shared values and objectives and define clear benefits and equal value for all partners. The Partnership will be based on mutual respect, trust and understanding, and above all, a commitment to progressive educational debate.
Become a Partnership School
We are keen to welcome schools from across different phases and types to join the Partnership and aim to work together to offer enhanced opportunities to all students across the network.
By becoming a member, you may offer your expertise or facilities to other schools in the group wherever it is possible to do so, helping to create a pool of resources across the region to assist in providing opportunity to every child. Whilst this is not an expectation and it is understood that there will be limitations in availability, finance and time, if we work together many obstacles can be overcome through a shared common goal.
To find out more about Schools in Partnership, email [email protected].

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing arts - St George’s School Windsor Castle
pageCache.text:
PERFORMING ARTS
Every child is exposed to music and drama, and we believe both are crucial to forming a rounded, ‘Real World Ready’ education.
Whether it be playing a musical instrument, involvement in one of our many ensembles and choirs, or taking part in our ambitious drama programme, we firmly believe in the skills obtained through involvement in performing arts.
Music
From the school’s foundation in 1348, music has been at its core and today this is still very much the case. With the majority of children having instrumental lessons at school, students are able to join a variety of instrumental ensembles and choirs, all of which perform regularly in St George’s Chapel.
There are informal instrumental concerts in the Pre-Prep and Prep School, and a number of instrumental ensembles for more senior students which provide further opportunities to practise and perform for an audience. Evening concerts are a wonderful opportunity for students to gain confidence and for parents and friends to enjoy the results of their hard work and practice.
Our state of the art recording and musical IT suite enables children to explore and incorporate composition and recording into their musical skills.
Choirs
Supers’ Choir
Numbering around 30 girls and boys from across the Prep School and Senior Prep, this large choir offers the chance to sing exciting repertoire, often in many parts. As well as singing regularly in Chapel, the choir sings for many concerts, including outside engagements. The choir is open to all children in Years 5–8 who wish to join, and rehearses weekly.
Chamber Choir
Singing for Chapel services and concerts alike, this smaller choir of around 25 children works at a more intense pace. The children rehearse several times weekly, all learning to read from musical scores to enable them to prepare music with a greater frequency. The choir performs across a range of local and national venues, including an annual Christmas concert in London, tours both in this country and abroad and regularly joins forces with other choral foundations.
T-Voices
Boys and girls in Years 3 and 4 can participate in this training choir. They come together weekly after school. Throughout rehearsals children learn the foundations of good vocal technique as they prepare for termly performances and other school engagements.
Speech and Drama
All students have the opportunity to take part in one or more of our drama productions during the course of the year.
There are annual Harvest and Christmas performances in the Pre-Prep which always receive warm applause. Students in Years 4 and 5 work together on a show, presented in December, and Year 6 presents a production in March each year, performed in Windsor’s Old Court Theatre. In Years 7 and 8 a Shakespeare production alternates with a larger-scale show.
All students are encouraged to take part in these productions, either on stage or back of house, in a technical or stage management role. Students of all ages also have an opportunity to take part in regular visiting drama workshops.
LAMDA
St George’s offers students the chance to study key performance and communication skills through Speech and Drama lessons, as part of the school’s co-curricular programme. Over the course of a year, students have the opportunity to enhance their technical performance and vocal technique as they prepare for graded LAMDA (London Academy of Music and Dramatic Arts) assessments. These weekly private lessons (taking place in either pair or solo format) are a superb way of supporting a student’s growth in confidence for the stage, in the classroom or for their future career.
For further information about the exciting world of LAMDA and the exams on offer at St George’s, please contact Amelia Voice at [email protected].

STAFF AND GOVERNORS
To achieve our vision of enabling our students to be ‘Real World Ready’, we have developed a faculty structure, which means that in addition to a dedicated body of staff in the Pre-Prep, Prep and Senior Prep, there are also a number of faculty specialists available across the school. In addition, all students are supported by the wellbeing team, comprised of staff from across the school.
The Senior Leadership Team
The Senior Leadership Team (SLT) have strategic and tactical oversight of the school and are responsible for leading on the strategy set.

The Pedagogical Leadership Team
The Pedagogical Leadership Team (PLT) supports the day-to-day running of the school, overall school improvement and monitors the effectiveness of the school’s development plan.
School Governors
The Board of Governors sets the strategy for the school, has financial oversight and monitors compliance, and delegates responsibility for the operational leadership and management to the Senior Leadership Team.
To get in touch with any of the governors, please email [email protected]. Emails to this address will be read in the first instance by the Clerk to the Governors, Katie Chorley and will be forwarded as appropriate.
The Right Reverend Dr Christopher Cocksworth
Educated at Manchester University and trained for ministry at St John’s College, Nottingham, Mr Dean was ordained in 1989. In 1992 he was appointed Chaplain at Royal Holloway, University of London and in 2001 Principal of Ridley Hall, University of Cambridge. Seven years later he became the Bishop of Coventry. He was installed as the 65th Dean of Windsor on 23 November 2023. Mr Dean is Chair of Council.
Tracey Blackley
Tracey is the most recent newly appointed governor, joining the Board in September 2023. A former St George’s parent, she has a wide range of business experience covering governance, risk and compliance as well as project/programme and bid management. Tracey has joined the Governance and Compliance Committee.
Ian Canning
Ian has enjoyed a varied career in HR at institutions including the Bank of England, the Zurich Insurance Company and Harlequins Rugby Club. He has previous experience as a prep school governor at the Cavendish School in Camden and also serves as a governor of the Royal School in Windsor Great Park. Ian chairs the Strategy and Development Committee and sits on the Finance and General Purposes Committee. He is also the Governor’s representative on the Parents’ Advisory Committee.
Julie Cornell
With expertise in alumni relations, development, fundraising and communications in independent schools, Julie chairs the Governance and Compliance Committee and sits on the Strategy and Development Committee.
James Dahl
James is Master of Wellington College, governor at two other prep schools and a trustee of both the UK’s largest exam board and the Old Wellingtonian Charitable Trust. Joining the Board of Governors at St George’s School in 2021, James brings his passion for holistic models of education and the transformative power of coeducation and boarding to the Council. James sits on the Education, Staffing and Music Committee and is the Round Square Governor.
Fabian French
Fabian is an alumnus of St George’s, with very happy memories of his time at the school. After a brief period as a corporate solicitor, he worked in corporate finance at leading City firms. In 2010, he moved into the charity sector: first as Fundraising Director at Marie Curie and then at UK Community Foundations as Chief Executive. He has various NED roles both in the for-profit and not-for-profit sectors. Fabian is a member of the Finance and General Purposes Committee, the Governance Committee and the Strategy Committee.
Helen Sandom
Helen joined the School Council in November 2016, bringing extensive experience in strategy, marketing and HR. A former St George’s parent, Helen has worked with a wide range of organisations, including St George’s House. Helen chairs the Finance and General Purposes Committee and sits on the Strategy and Development Committee.
Jane Scott
Jane retired as Head of The Granville School in 2018 after ten years in post. For many years Jane served on various IAPS committees, acting as a mentor to new Head Teachers and chairing the IAPS charitable activities body, the iTrust. Jane was a qualified ISI team inspector. Jane has a particular love of music, being a singer and board member of the Bach Choir.
Claire Robinson
Following 16 years as Executive Headteacher at Holme Grange School, during which the school grew from 200 to nearly 800 students, Claire now acts as an educational consultant for a range of organisations including MTM Consulting, as well as an assessor for NACE. Claire sits on the Education and Strategy and Development Committees.
Canon Nick Brown
Prior to joining the College of St George as the Canon Steward, Nick had been Precentor and Subdean of Lincoln, having served in parishes in Lincolnshire and Wiltshire. He has wider interests that include music and railways, and he has undertaken research into the relationship between music and theology. Nick sits on the Finance and General Purpose Committee
Lieutenant General Philip Jones
Phil Jones served for 36 years in the British Army, departing the Service in 2016 as a Lieutenant General. With over 15 international operational deployments, including three secondments to leadership roles in the UN and two to NATO, he gained operational experience in most of the major military campaigns of the past 30+ years. He served for over 3.5 years in Afghanistan. In May 2022 Phil was appointed by the late Queen Elizabeth II to be Constable and Governor of Windsor Castle. Phil sits on the Strategy and Development committee.

St George’s to join the St Albans Education Group and partner with St George’s Ascot to create a new co-educational through school
We are delighted to share that St George’s School Windsor Castle will be joining the St Albans Education Group (STAEG) in Summer 2026. STAEG is a growing group of independent schools united by a shared commitment to educational excellence, outstanding pastoral care and forward-thinking leadership. Becoming part of this well-respected charitable group will provide St George’s with greater strength, stability and opportunities for collaboration.
We are also excited by a closer partnership with St George’s Ascot following their announcement in January that they too will be joining STAEG. Together we are pleased to propose the creation of a new, co-educational through school.
The new through school, St George’s School, Windsor and Ascot, will offer a seamless educational journey from ages 3 to 18 with access to excellent facilities across two sites. The Kindergarten, Pre-Prep, Prep and Senior Prep to Year 8 will remain at Windsor, ensuring continuity and a strong foundation through early and middle years. From Year 9, students will then have the opportunity to continue their education at the Ascot site, just a short 15-minute journey away, through to A levels. St George’s Ascot is known for outstanding academic outcomes, with value-added GCSE performance that places the school among the top 3% nationally. St George’s Ascot is also looking ahead to becoming co-educational, welcoming boys into Years 7 and 9 from September 2027.
We have much in common with St George’s Ascot beyond our names. We both have long and proud histories, strong academic and co-curricular traditions, particularly in music and the creative arts, and both schools offer flexible boarding that reflects the needs of modern families. Just as importantly, our ethos, values and vision align, inspired as they are by St George, the great Christian saint, and there is a real sense of shared purpose about the future. Our Heads, Emma Károlyi and Hannah Fox, bring a wealth of experience, and are genuinely excited about working together to build something distinctive and enduring.
We take great pride in our school’s history and our ongoing role within the College of St George, and we will continue to educate the choristers of St George’s Chapel. Becoming part of STAEG and joining with St George’s Ascot to form the new St George’s School, Windsor and Ascot will allow us to build a strong and sustainable future, while staying true to all that makes St George’s so special.
“This is an extremely exciting step forward for St George’s School Windsor Castle. Joining together with St George’s Ascot to create an excellent through school from early years to sixth form, not only provides continuity but opens up enriching new opportunities for our students and staff, while preserving our rich history and the very special nature, values and vision of both schools. As part of STAEG, we will benefit from the strength, stability and shared expertise of a wider group, including investing in our people, increasing our provision and securing the future of the school.”
– Emma Károlyi, Head of St George’s School Windsor Castle
“We’re delighted to welcome St George’s Windsor into STAEG. It’s a co-educational school with a proud heritage and values that closely align with our own. Bringing Windsor and Ascot together creates a genuinely exciting opportunity to build a seamless, high-quality education for girls and boys from early years through to sixth form, while strengthening what already makes both schools so special.”
– Amber Waite, Principal of STAEG

pageCache.text:
SCHOLARSHIPS
Thanks to generous support from the Andrew Lloyd Webber Foundation, we are delighted to be able to offer a small number of transformative music scholarships commencing in September 2026. Upon joining the school in Year 4, scholarship recipients will each receive funding for five years, covering up to 100% of school fees in addition to weekly music tuition for two instruments. They will also have the opportunity to join the wide variety of instrumental ensembles and school choirs available at St George’s, taking part in regular performances throughout the school year.
Applications are welcome from families of students currently in Year 3 who have demonstrated or expressed a keen interest in music. Awarded on the combined basis of merit and financial need, the scholarships aim to broaden access to the exceptional all-round education on offer at St George’s. Please note that this will require parents to be means-tested as part of the selection process and that the opportunity is open only to families with no current connection to the school.
In the first instance, interested families are warmly invited to register for a place at our upcoming scholarship auditions, which will be held at St George’s on Monday 9 and/or Tuesday 10 February. While children take part in their audition, parents will have the opportunity to learn more about the scholarships on offer and the next steps in the application process, an outline of which is below. NB: APPLICATIONS FOR THE FEBRUARY AUDITIONS ARE NOW CLOSED. DETAILS OF ANY FUTURE AUDITIONS WILL BE POSTED ON THIS PAGE IN DUE COURSE, SHOULD PLACES STILL BE AVAILABLE AFTER THE AUDITIONS IN FEBRUARY.
APPLICATION PROCESS AND FAQs
Please review the information below regarding the application process and the opportunity on offer. Further information and the opportunity to ask more in-depth questions will be provided at the auditions in February. Alternatively, please contact our Registrar, Aileen De Vally-King: [email protected].
The application process for a music scholarship commencing in September 2026 will follow a number of steps, as below:
1. Interested families are required to register to attend a scholarship audition which will take place on either Monday 9 and/or Tuesday 10 February (depending on applicant numbers). While at St George’s, students will take part in an audition, while parents will have the opportunity to learn more about what a music scholarship at St George’s would entail. To register for this event, please complete the form above.
2. Following the initial audition, successful families will be invited to complete a formal application, including submitting information to our independent bursary assessment organisation to assess their financial suitability for the scholarship. TRIPS AND RESIDENTIALS
Educational visits are an integral part of the learning experience for students at St George’s and during the course of the year students enjoy a variety of day trips to historic sites, farms, museums, theatres and galleries.
As a proud member school of Round Square, adventure sits right at the heart of our educational journey. Residential experiences are proven to develop powerful skills such as collaboration, problem solving, communication as well as securing confidence and a growth mindset.
Students in Year 4 and 5 undertake a residential trip at the end of the summer term, where they are gently nurtured out of their comfort zone. In Year 6, our students go on a PGL adventure trip, where, in addition to a raft of engaging activities, they are challenged to think for themselves, help one another and achieve something they didn’t feel they might be able to.
In Years 7 and 8, students spend a week in the far north-west coast of Scotland at the Ridgway Adventure Centre, where they pursue the John Muir Award. The final night is spent on ‘survival island’ and involves the groups navigating complex decisions and tasks. In alternate years, the group will spend a week in Spain on an adventure course.

pageCache.text:
CHORISTERS
Since its foundation in 1352, St George’s has been a Choir School and home to the choristers who sing in the choir of St George’s Chapel in Windsor Castle.
This musical tradition is as vibrant and important today as it ever was and the choristers, although only small in number in our school community, fulfil a vital role in the daily life of the school and the college.
The choir is formed of up to 23 choristers, both boys and girls, with new choristers – some of whom may already be students at the school – appointed during Year 3 to begin with the choir at the start of Year 4. If vacancies exist in older year groups, it may be possible for a child to join as a chorister at a later date. Choristers remain in the choir until the end of Year 8, when they leave St George’s for senior school.
In addition to the excellent musical grounding that they receive from the Chapel Director of Music, the Assistant Director of Music and Organ Scholar, they receive regular singing lessons with the renowned teacher, Anita Morrison. Within the School, choristers also take music theory lessons and learn to play at least two instruments.
The choristers live in the School’s boarding house from Sunday morning to Friday evening, rehearsing every morning and singing in services on most days as well as on special occasions such as Garter Day, and over Christmas and Easter.
A choristership is an intense but rewarding and enjoyable experience which gives students confidence, poise and the ability to work in a team.

PARENTS
A positive, proactive and trusting relationship between the school and our families is paramount in ensuring the happiness and success of every child’s learning and wellbeing experience at St George’s. We pride ourselves on our sense of community and the rapport we build with our parent body, as well as the unwavering dedication shown by our parents to engage in all areas of school life.
PARENT PORTAL AND TODDLE
St George’s Parent Portal is a secure online access point for parents to view information relating to their child or children at St George’s, including activities bookings, account balances and contact details. The Portal helps us to reduce the amount of paper we send home from school and helps us to lessen our environmental footprint.
Toddle is an interactive platform for reporting, calendar management, updates and information. It enables greater two-way communication between parents and teachers and provides a repository for end of term reports, which are uploaded to Toddle for parents to view. As our main method of communication, we encourage parents to check Toddle regularly.
Details of how to access both Toddle and the Parent Portal are shared with parents as their child joins the school. Any current parents requiring assistance are welcome to contact the school office: [email protected].
Parents’ group
The Parents’ Group is a small team of parent volunteers that plays a vital role here at St George’s. Its annual calendar of events aims to bring everyone at the school together in a fun and relaxed way, whilst raising money for charity and important school projects. They provide the social glue that helps us maintain the friendly and collaborative atmosphere that everyone here at St George’s is so proud of.
In recent years, proceeds from Parent’s Group initiatives have been donated to charities including Thames Hospice, School in a Bag and Action for Children, as well as contributing to some fantastic additional facilities around the school, such as our sports pavilion in Home Park Private.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performance - St George’s School Windsor Castle
pageCache.text:
PERFORMANCE
Engagement with parents sits at the heart of our aim to foster an environment of high performance. Within our curriculum framework, parents are encouraged to become fully involved in their child’s learning process, and the school works closely with them to achieve the best outcomes for every student.
Full, written reports are provided at the end of each term, with room for student reflections. Specific targets are provided to enable the students to progressively raise their performance.
In addition, each term parents are invited to spend time in their child’s classroom to look over their work and share in their progress.
Parent Teacher meetings are held in Autumn and Spring. In Years 7 and 8, students lead their meetings to foster a sense of self-regulation.
Student progress is monitored at all times by the teacher, head of faculty and the learning enrichment team. Standardised testing is undertaken twice a year, and whilst it contributes to the overall picture, much more thorough is the day-to-day monitoring and encouragement given by the teachers to every student.
Rather than using terms like ‘ability’ and ‘potential’, both of which compartmentalise students into predetermined groups, we refer to student progress as performance. By fostering a highly ambitious environment where every student can achieve at a high level, we are not limiting their success. Rather than judge a student against their peers, their performance is judged against their own prior performance, thus providing them the stimulus to set their own high targets.

PRE-PREP
At St George’s Pre-Prep we are proud of our vibrant and happy community where children are given the space and freedom to learn. Our approach to teaching, both inside and outside the classroom, is designed to inspire, challenge and engage each and every child to make the most of their talents and potential. Our experienced teachers, broad range of subjects and activities and spacious, purpose-built classrooms enable us to achieve this.
Developing vital skills
Teaching and learning of key skills and knowledge is delivered through a cross curricular, multi-disciplinary approach. Other areas such as phonics, letter formation and number skills will be taught in the form of a ‘lesson’ with a specific focus or learning objective. We follow Read Write Inc throughout the Pre-Prep and through this programme the children will develop the vital skills they need for reading, spelling and writing.
Mathematical learning
From Reception, children begin the building of mathematical knowledge and this is continued throughout the Pre-Prep. Children are immersed in blocks of learning focusing on all key mathematical concepts including number, shape, space and measure. Longer blocks of learning allow teachers to really develop problem solving and mastery approaches which are vital for increased understanding and future mathematical learning. Children are then given many opportunities to practise, develop, extend and reinforce their emerging skills during the rest of the day in play situations.
